title: Verify the guided questionnaire is offered to a new seeker on their first visit from the home page
description: This test ensures that the primary entry point for preference capture is presented to new, anonymous users as intended, which is critical for the user acquisition and engagement strategy. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: As a first-time visitor to the job platform, I expect to be presented with a clear and immediate option to start a guided questionnaire from the home page, so I can provide my job preferences without having to search for the feature.
prerequisites: User must be a new visitor, meaning no existing session cookies or account data for the platform are present in the browser. The feature flag for the guided questionnaire must be enabled.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open a new browser in incognito or private mode to ensure a clean session.
2. Navigate to the application's home page URL.
3. Observe the main content area of the home page upon loading.
4. Verify that a prominent banner, modal, or section is displayed, inviting the user to start the guided questionnaire.
5. Click the 'Start' or equivalent button to begin the questionnaire.
6. Verify that the first question of the questionnaire is displayed, confirming the flow has been initiated.
7. Close the browser tab.
8. Open a new tab in the same private session and navigate to the home page again.
9. Verify that the questionnaire prompt is still visible, indicating the anonymous session state is maintained.
expectedResult:
1. A guided questionnaire is offered to the user on the home page during their first visit.
2. The user can successfully initiate the questionnaire from the home page prompt.
3. The system correctly identifies the user as a new visitor and triggers the onboarding workflow.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Collect the seeker's requirements through a short guided questionnaire offered from the home page on a first visit, before any account exists.

9. Verify that the 'Location: United States' filter tag remains active and applied to the results.
expectedResult:

2. The job results list updates in real-time to reflect the broader search.
3. All other active preference filters remain unchanged and continue to be applied.

title: Verify the system indicates which specific constraint is narrowing the results set when very few listings are returned
description: This test ensures the platform provides helpful feedback to the user when their search is too restrictive, improving usability and preventing user frustration. Automation: MEDIUM (may require specific data setup and UI element verification).
testDescription: A job seeker combines several niche preferences, such as a very high salary, a specific non-technical job title, and a remote-only requirement for a small country. This combination returns zero or one job. The system should guide the user on which filter to adjust.
prerequisites: The test environment's job database is seeded in a way that a specific combination of filters will result in 0 or <3 results. For example, many 'Marketing Manager' roles exist, but only one is 'fully remote' in 'New Zealand' with a salary over '$200,000'.
stepsToPerform:
1. As an anonymous user, complete the preference questionnaire.
2. Set 'Job Title' to 'Marketing Manager'.
3. Set 'Working Arrangement' to 'fully remote'.
4. Set 'Location' to 'New Zealand'.
5. Set 'Annual Salary' to target '$200,000'.
6. Submit the preferences and navigate to the job results page.
7. Observe that the number of results is very low (e.g., 'Showing 1 result').
8. Scan the page for a notification, banner, or tooltip providing feedback.
9. Verify a message is displayed, such as 'Very few jobs match all your preferences. Try widening your 'Location' or 'Salary' to see more.'
10. Confirm the message correctly identifies the most restrictive filters.
expectedResult:
1. When a combination of preferences returns a very low number of listings, a clear message is displayed to the user.
2. The message correctly identifies at least one of the specific preferences that is most significantly narrowing the result set.
3. The system does not crash or show a generic 'no results' error without context.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Where a combination of preferences returns very few listings, indicate which constraint is narrowing the set.

title: Verify captured preferences are applied to searches on later visits once a user account exists
description: This test validates the persistence of user preferences across sessions for registered users, a key feature for a personalized experience. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: A registered user set their job preferences to 'Fully Remote' and 'USA' during a visit yesterday. Today, when they log back into the site, they expect to immediately see jobs matching those saved preferences without having to re-enter them.
prerequisites: A user account exists in the database (e.g., 'test.seeker.p0@example.com'). This account has preferences saved from a previous session: 'Working Arrangement: Fully Remote' and 'Location: USA'.
stepsToPerform:
1. In a new, clean browser session, navigate to the platform's login page.
2. Enter the credentials for the user 'test.seeker.p0@example.com' and click 'Log In'.
3. After successful login, navigate directly to the main job search page (or observe the default landing page if it shows jobs).
4. Do not enter any new search terms or filters.
5. Observe the list of jobs presented on the page.
6. Locate the 'Active Filters' section of the UI.
7. Verify that the filters 'Working Arrangement: Fully Remote' and 'Location: USA' are displayed as active.
8. Inspect the top 5 job listings to confirm they are all remote roles based in the USA.
9. Log out of the account to end the session.
expectedResult:
1. Upon logging in, the user's saved preferences from previous sessions are automatically loaded and applied.
2. The initial job search results are filtered based on these persistent preferences.
3. The UI clearly indicates which saved filters are currently active.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Apply the captured preferences... to later visits once an account exists.

title: Verify the personalized job listings are ranked against the seeker's captured preferences
description: This test ensures the job matching algorithm is functioning correctly by prioritizing and ranking the most relevant jobs higher in the results list. Automation: MEDIUM (requires a controlled data set and may be hard to assert ranking perfectly).
testDescription: A seeker specifies they are looking for a 'Senior Product Manager' role targeting a '$150,000' salary. The system should show a job titled 'Senior Product Manager' at '$155,000' before a job titled 'Product Manager' at '$120,000', assuming all other factors are equal.
prerequisites: The job database is seeded with a controlled set of jobs. For a search for 'Senior Product Manager, $150k', the DB contains: Job A ('Senior Product Manager', $155k), Job B ('Product Manager', $150k), and Job C ('Senior Product Manager', $125k).
stepsToPerform:
1. As an anonymous user, complete the preference questionnaire.
2. Set 'Job Title' to 'Senior Product Manager'.
3. Set 'Target Salary' to '$150,000'.
4. Set any other required preferences to be identical for all test jobs.
5. Submit the preferences and view the job results page.
6. Ensure the results are sorted by 'Relevance' (the default).
7. Observe the order of the jobs in the list.
8. Verify that Job A (perfect title match, close salary) appears higher than Job B (imperfect title match, perfect salary).
9. Verify that Job A also appears higher than Job C (perfect title match, distant salary).
expectedResult:
1. The job results are displayed in a ranked order based on relevance to the user's preferences.
2. Listings that are a stronger match across multiple preferences (e.g., job title, salary) are ranked higher than those with weaker matches.
3. The default sort order for personalized results is 'Relevance'.

sourceCitation.excerpt: filtered and ranked against those preferences.

title: Verify an anonymous user can complete the questionnaire and view matched results without an account or payment
description: This test validates the core value proposition of the onboarding flow: an anonymous user can see personalized results before committing to registration. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: A new visitor lands on the homepage and is curious about the platform. They want to see what kind of jobs are available for them by answering a few questions, without the friction of creating an account or providing payment details.
prerequisites: User is a new visitor with no existing account, session cookies, or local storage data for the site. The site is publicly accessible.

3. Observe the prompt to start the guided questionnaire.

5. Proceed through the questionnaire, selecting 'fully remote' for working arrangement and '$80,000' for target salary.
6. Complete all steps of the questionnaire.
7. Click the final submission button (e.g., 'See My Matched Jobs').

9. Verify that no registration modal, login page, or payment screen was presented at any point.
10. Confirm that a list of job postings is visible and they are relevant to the preferences entered.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Browsing listings, completing the questionnaire and viewing matched results require no account and no payment.

title: Verify registration is requested only when an anonymous seeker attempts to apply for a listing
description: This test confirms that the registration gate is correctly placed, triggering only on a high-intent action ('Apply') as specified. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: An anonymous user has found a job they are interested in after completing the questionnaire. They can view all the details, but when they decide to apply, the system should prompt them to create an account to proceed.
prerequisites: An anonymous user has successfully completed the preference questionnaire and is on the job results page. At least one job listing is displayed.
stepsToPerform:

2. Observe that the job detail page loads and all information is visible. Confirm no registration is requested at this stage.
3. Navigate back to the results page.
4. Locate the 'Apply' button on the first job listing in the list view.
5. Click the 'Apply' button.
6. Observe the system's response.
7. Verify that a registration/login modal or page is immediately displayed.
8. Confirm that the application process does not proceed further until the user signs up or logs in.
expectedResult:
1. Viewing job listings and details does not trigger a registration prompt.
2. Clicking the 'Apply' button immediately gates the user with a registration/login prompt.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Registration is requested only when the seeker acts on a listing — applying, saving it, or setting up alerts.

title: Verify all preferences captured before registration successfully carry over into the new account upon sign-up
description: This test validates the critical state transition from an anonymous user with session-based data to a registered user with persisted data. It ensures no information is lost during the conversion, which is essential for a seamless user experience and immediate personalization of the new account. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: As a new user, I want to fill out the job preference questionnaire, and then sign up for an account. I expect all the answers I just provided to be automatically saved to my new profile so I don't have to enter them again.
prerequisites: User must be a new visitor with no existing session cookies. The backend job database must contain listings that match the preferences to be selected.
stepsToPerform:

2. Observe the guided questionnaire prompt and begin the process.

11. After successful registration, log in and navigate to the 'My Preferences' or 'Profile' page.
expectedResult:
1. The user's profile page displays all the preferences that were entered during the anonymous session.
2. The 'working arrangement' is 'fully remote', 'annual salary' is '125000', 'location' is 'United States', and 'category' is 'Software Development'.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Preferences captured before registration carry over into the account when the seeker signs up.

title: Verify an uploaded resume from an anonymous session is retained and associated with the new account after registration
description: This test ensures that user-uploaded documents, specifically a resume, persist across the anonymous-to-registered state transition. This prevents critical data loss and user frustration, ensuring the resume is immediately available for applications. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: As a new user, I want to upload my resume during the initial onboarding process. If I then decide to create an account to save a job, I expect my uploaded resume to be automatically linked to my new account without needing to upload it again.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Hold preferences and uploaded documents against the seeker for the duration of an anonymous visit, and against the account thereafter.

title: Verify a registered user can revisit and change their preferences without having to repeat the whole questionnaire
description: This test confirms that registered users can efficiently manage their job preferences by editing individual items. This improves usability by avoiding the need to restart the entire onboarding process for a small change. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: As a registered user, my job search needs may change over time. I want to be able to go into my account settings and update a single preference, like my target salary, without being forced to go through all the original onboarding questions again.
prerequisites: An active, registered user account exists (e.g., 'test+user01@example.com'). This account has a pre-existing, complete set of job preferences, including a target salary of '$80,000'.

8. Observe a success message confirming the update.
9. Refresh the page and verify the new salary value is displayed.

title: Verify a registered user can successfully remove their uploaded resume from their profile
description: This test validates a key data privacy and user control feature. It ensures users can permanently delete their personal documents from the system, which is a common requirement for data protection compliance. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: As a registered user, I want to have full control over my documents. If I no longer want my resume stored on the platform, I need a clear and effective way to remove it from my profile.

5. Locate and click the 'Remove' or 'Delete' icon/button next to the resume file name.
6. A confirmation dialog appears asking 'Are you sure you want to remove this resume?'. Click 'Confirm' or 'Yes'.

8. Refresh the page or navigate away and back to the document management section.
expectedResult:

title: Verify a registered user can successfully clear all their saved job preferences
description: This test ensures users can exercise their right to data erasure by clearing all preference data. This is a critical feature for data privacy compliance and gives users ultimate control over their personal information. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: As a registered user, I may want to start my job search over from scratch or remove my data from the platform. I expect to find an option to clear all my saved preferences at once, returning my profile to a default state.

title: Verify that after clearing preferences, subsequent job searches are no longer filtered by the old preferences

testDescription: As a user, after I clear my preferences, I expect my next job search to be broad and unfiltered. The system should not remember or use my old, deleted preferences to narrow down the results.
prerequisites: A registered user account ('test+user04@example.com') exists. The job database contains a wide variety of jobs across different locations and categories.

expectedResult:

description: This audit test confirms that removing a resume fully disassociates it from all user-facing workflows. It ensures the deleted document cannot be accidentally attached to applications or used by backend matching algorithms, protecting user privacy. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: As a user, once I delete my resume from my profile, I have a strong expectation that it is truly gone. It should not appear as an option when I apply for a job, and the system should not use its contents to suggest jobs to me.
prerequisites: A registered user account ('test+user05@example.com') exists with a resume ('resume_to_audit.pdf') already uploaded.

expectedResult:

2. The user is prompted to upload a new resume to proceed with the application.
3. Any job matching or recommendation algorithms that use resume content no longer factor in the deleted resume's data.

title: Verify a user who gets few results sees the narrowing constraint message, widens the filter, and successfully registers with the updated preferences
description: This end-to-end test validates the user feedback loop for overly restrictive searches. It ensures the system correctly identifies the constraining filter, allows the user to correct it, and saves the updated, more effective preferences upon registration. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: As a new user, if I am too specific with my search criteria and get no results, I want the system to tell me which filter is causing the problem. I should be able to easily adjust that filter, see better results, and then sign up with my corrected preferences saved.
prerequisites: User is a new visitor. The job database is populated such that a specific combination of filters (e.g., Job Title: 'Lead Shuttle-Driver, Martian Colony') will yield zero results.

2. The user can successfully modify the filter on the results page.
3. The newly created account has all preferences saved *except* for the restrictive job title that was cleared.
